description: Grants permission to read code files and explore directory structures within the assigned session workspace.
Grants permission to create, edit, and update code files within allowed workspace paths.
Grants permission to remove files or empty directories inside the workspace.
Permission to initialize, switch, and clean up isolated Git worktrees for agent tasks.
Permission to generate and read unified diffs between the working tree and base branches.
Permission to stage changes (git add) and create local commits within the worktree branch.
Permission to execute arbitrary shell commands inside the secure, isolated container sandbox.
Scoped permission to trigger unit tests and test runners (e.g., npm test, pytest, mvn test).
Scoped permission to run project builds and compilation tools.
Permission for the primary orchestrator model to invoke and coordinate helper sub-agents.
Permission to query repositories, issues, PRs, and commit history via GitHub MCP servers.
Permission to search and read Jira tickets, epics, and requirements.
Permission to execute read-only SQL queries against registered internal test/dev databases.
Permission to run static code analysis tools (e.g., ESLint, Checkstyle, SonarQube CLI, Prettier).
Permission to execute security scanners (e.g., Snyk, Trivy, OWASP Dependency-Check) on the workspace.
Permission to read dependency manifests (package.json, pom.xml, go.mod, requirements.txt).
Permission to execute package manager installations (e.g., npm install, mvn dependency:resolve, pip install).
Permission to execute Node.js scripts, build tools (Webpack, Vite), or TypeScript compilation (tsc).
Permission to run Java compilation, Maven goals (mvn clean compile), or Gradle tasks.
Permission to execute Python scripts, virtual environments, or dependency management (poetry, pipenv).
Permission to build container images (docker build) or inspect Dockerfiles and Compose configs.
Permission to run database migration tools (e.g., Liquibase, Flyway, Prisma) against dev/test databases.
Permission to parse code Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs) to analyze class hierarchies, method signatures, and symbol references across files.
Permission to generate or update OpenAPI specifications, GraphQL schemas, gRPC protos, database entities, and DTO structures.
Permission to generate C4 architectural models, PlantUML diagrams, or Architecture Decision Record (ADR) documentation.
Permission to scan codebases against defined structural rules (e.g., preventing domain layers from depending on infrastructure layers, detecting cyclic dependencies).
Permission to execute complex, multi-file refactoring operations (e.g., interface extraction, package reorganization, global renaming).
Permission to automatically generate comprehensive unit tests (JUnit, Jest, PyTest), mock objects, and test fixtures for implemented features.
Permission to read, update, tag, and draft replies in customer ticketing and CRM systems (e.g., Zendesk, Salesforce Service Cloud).
Permission to evaluate customer messages for tone, urgency, churn risk, and escalation triggers.
Permission to query internal documentation, support articles, and FAQ repositories for approved answers.
Permission to inspect monitoring alerts, error logs, and metrics (e.g., Datadog, PagerDuty) to diagnose system outages.
Permission to trigger pre-approved operational remediation scripts or diagnostic commands.
Permission to review or initiate user access requests, permission audits, or SSO group lookups.
Permission to execute read-only analytics queries against data warehouses (e.g., Snowflake, BigQuery, PostgreSQL analytics DBs).
Permission to aggregate metrics, summarize KPI trends, and compile structured business briefing documents.
Permission to scan contracts, PRDs, or architecture documents against regulatory standards (e.g., GDPR, ISO 27001, internal policies).
Permission to query internal employee handbooks and benefits portals to answer HR inquiries accurately.
